svg.text: W10 rev. 2 · Themes, templates, images and the three outputs (web, email, PDF) · AWK-17 · 2026-10-14
A look is data: tokens (colours, font, corners), images and a layout preset. One renderer per output maps the same data; nothing is web-only CSS.

F · rev. 2 · Images placed on purpose, backgrounds, and styling that reaches every output · EN

F2 · Background, in the theme (and per page)
Contrast is checked on text over the
Behind the content column; content cards stay readable (surface colour, optional transparency).
F3 · Styling in the theme: the same values drive web, email and PDF
F4 · How each output draws it
* background images show where the mail client supports them; the colour always.

1 Themes belong to the organisation; one is the default. Presets are starting points: Werkstatt, Klar (calm, light), Warm (soft colours, rounded), Kontrast (AAA). A survey uses the default unless B picks another.

2 Colours are checked on save: text and button contrast at least WCAG AA, also over background images with their overlay; below that the theme is not saved. Fonts: a fixed set of self-hosted OFL fonts.

3 Layout presets place logo, header image and content: Card, Header image, Split image (image beside the questions on wide screens, above on phones), Minimal. Email and PDF map each preset to their own layout.
4 The preview shows the same survey in Web, Email and PDF, so a theme is never judged on the web alone. Images are stored in the organisation's file storage (folder or S3), resized on upload.

5 Per survey: pick a theme and an own header image with alt text per language. 6 Templates: Askwerk's own and the organisation's (Save as template in the designer's menu); creating copies the definition.
7 Messages: invitation, reminder, thank-you and result PDF texts per language with placeholders; the first question can be answered in the email (rating, NPS, yes/no, single choice), as links.

8 Email: table layout and inline styles, no JS. PDF: A4/Letter, page numbers, a QR code to the online survey; fillable PDF fields later. Emoji faces are drawn as images in email and PDF, so they look the same.

9 Images placed on purpose: an Image block (size, alignment, caption, alt text required per language), picture choices for single and multiple choice, and an image beside a question. Part of the survey definition.

10 Backgrounds: colour, image, or image with a colour overlay; cover, contain or tile; in the theme and per page. 11 Styling tokens (fonts, scale, spacing, buttons, cards, answer controls, progress) drive all three outputs.

12 Decided (Dražan, 2026-10-14): PDF option (a), our own renderer in .NET (PdfSharp/MigraDoc, MIT), styled fully from the theme, with images and backgrounds. Custom CSS stays a flagged extra for the web only.
Open for Dražan: fonts — a fixed set of self-hosted fonts (recommended), or also font files uploaded by the organisation (licence is then their responsibility)?
